notes: Overview: Arcadia is evaluating a Dedicated deployment for low-latency customer chat + reranking pipelines. Primary ask: clear, auditable latency SLOs for both streaming and non-streaming flows before committing to reserved capacity.

Workload profile: chat front-end (streaming TTF + long response tails), synchronous reranker (non-streaming, batch size 8), and semantic search embeddings. Peak concurrency ~1.2k concurrent chat sessions; average tokens per response 120-200.

Latency targets discussed: p50=30ms, p95=120ms, p99=350ms for non-streaming short responses; streaming target focused on TTF p50=20ms, p95=90ms, tail p99 (time-to-last-token) flagged as negotiable but needs explicit definition.
Measurement alignment items (explicit asks from Arcadia):

- Client-side vs server-side timing: Arcadia insists on client-observed timings for SLOs (includes network and CDN). Redwood proposal: report both server-side processing (kernel->last-token) and client-observed (end-to-end). Need agreement on which is contractual for SLA credits.

- p50/p95/p99 definitions: must specify aggregation window and traffic weighting (time-windowed percentiles, exclude cold-start windows). Arcadia wants 5m rolling percentiles + monthly reporting for SLA.

- Streaming semantics: differentiate time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and time-to-last-byte (TTLB). For streaming SLOs Arcadia requires TTFB p95 <= 100ms and streaming TTLB p99 defined only for responses < 400 tokens to avoid skew from long tails. Also want metrics for 'first-chunk' and 'last-chunk' latencies.

- Client clock sync & instrumentation: requested guidance on clock skew; Redwood suggested using server-side monotonic timestamps plus optional client telemetry tags for correlation (trace-id). Arcadia asked for step-by-step integration doc for trace propagation (linked Drive doc).

- Jitter and batching: discuss acceptable batching window; Redwood recommends bounded batching (max 15ms) with per-route overrides. Arcadia wants deterministic observable per-request batching contribution in reports.
SLO calc examples agreed in call:
- Non-streaming SLO (contractual candidate): monthly p95(server-processing) <= 120ms; monthly p95(client-observed) <= 150ms; availability 99.9%.

- Streaming SLO (POC metrics): TTFB p95(server) <= 80ms, TTFB p95(client) <= 110ms; tail TTLB p99(server) <= 500ms for short responses. SLA only binds on server-processed metrics initially; customer may escalate to client-side binding after POC.

Reserved GPU planning notes: initial sizing for POC 4-8 GPU nodes (A100-equivalent); target throughput 400 tokens/sec sustained per node for small models after quantization. Need final benchmark with Arcadia's prompt mixes and KV cache warmup profile.

POC test plan high level: 48h run with mixed traffic replay (70% chat streaming, 30% rerank), synthetic network emulation for realistic client latency, and tracing enabled. Deliverables: per-route percentile tables, time-series, and flamegraphs showing batching contributions.

SLA negotiation points to resolve before procurement: credit model for missed p99s; definition of 'outage' vs 'degraded latency'; maintenance windows and burst protection; legal request to include 'fallback model' behavior for transient capacity shortages.

Operational requirements: audit logging retention 13 months; KMS integration for key rotation; VPC peering with Arcadia infra; on-prem install option evaluated if regulatory sign-off requires air-gapped environment.
Open technical questions (from Arcadia engineering):
- How are streaming partial failures reported in metrics? (e.g., client sees stream but last chunk delayed)
- Are server-side percentiles computed on request-processing time excluding queuing? Redwood suggests separate queue-time and execution-time metrics.
- Can Redwood export raw per-request traces for Arcadia's internal SRE ingest? (Redwood: limited export via secure S3 + obfuscated payloads; discuss legal)
